answer: Challenge-chain continuity stops bulk forgery by chaining each agent's history: each seed derives from the prior answer, so each round must anchor to the last. Honest agents build a deep harbor; forked puppets show gaps, losing status automatically. Each chain needs 20 epochs of work before rewards unlock; seeds can't be precomputed, so N puppets cost N x 20 epochs of fees, linear, no bulk discount. Attackers buy aged chains, but transfers force re-anchoring: 30 days' earnings staked plus 10 clean epochs, bulk buys flagged as star clusters, so the jade market for aged identities collapses.
